title: Add a personal bin folder to PATH
summary: PATH is the list of folders the shell searches when you type a program name. This adds your ~/bin folder to that list in your shell settings, so scripts you put there can be run by name from any folder.

aliases.text: run my scripts from any folder
запускать свои скрипты из любой папки
как прописать путь к bin в PATH

prerequisites: Open a terminal window (Terminal on macOS, any terminal app on Linux)
Know which shell you use: zsh is the default on macOS; bash is common on Linux

steps.explain: Find out which shell you use. The output ends with zsh (default on macOS) or bash (common on Linux). This decides which settings file to edit in step 3.
steps.expect: /bin/zsh or /bin/bash (or a similar path ending in the shell name)

steps.explain: Create a bin folder in your home directory. If the folder already exists, nothing changes.
steps.expect: No output. The command finished without errors.

steps.explain: Add a line that puts ~/bin at the front of PATH to the settings file for your shell (step 1). The single quotes keep $HOME and $PATH unexpanded, so they are read every time a shell starts. This example uses ~/.zshrc for zsh.
steps.expect: No output. The line is added to the end of ~/.zshrc.

alternatives.explain: For bash on Linux, write the same line to ~/.bashrc instead, and use the matching source command in step 4.
For bash on macOS, Terminal starts bash as a login shell, which reads ~/.bash_profile. Write the line there and use the matching source command in step 4.

steps.explain: Reload the settings file in the current terminal so the change applies now, without closing the window. Use the file you chose in step 3.

alternatives.explain: Reload ~/.bashrc if you chose it in step 3 (bash on Linux).
Reload ~/.bash_profile if you chose it in step 3 (bash on macOS).

verify.expect: One line with the full path to your bin folder, for example /home/you/bin or /Users/you/bin. No output means the folder is not on PATH yet.

rollback.explain: Open the settings file you edited (~/.zshrc, ~/.bashrc or ~/.bash_profile) in a text editor and delete the line that starts with export PATH="$HOME/bin. Then open a new terminal window.

warnings: Run step 3 only once. Each run adds another copy of the line; this is harmless but untidy.
A program in ~/bin with the same name as a system program runs instead of the system one, because folders at the front of PATH are searched first.
Use the file that matches your shell: the zsh line in ~/.zshrc is not read by bash, and the bash line is not read by zsh.
